title: The Lie Algebra of XY-mixer Topologies and Warm Starting QAOA for Constrained Optimization
abstract_summary: The paper analyzes dynamical Lie algebras (DLAs) arising from various XY-mixer topologies used in QAOA for cardinality-constrained optimization, proving that 1D path/cycle mixers with only single-qubit Z rotations yield polynomial-sized DLAs while all-to-all XY connectivity or inclusion of RZZ terms produces exponentially large DLAs. Leveraging this algebraic structure, the authors propose a warm-starting strategy that pretrains a restricted, efficiently trainable ansatz (within a polynomial DLA) and then transfers parameters to the full circuit, demonstrating improved convergence and solution quality on constrained optimization tasks (Portfolio Optimization, Sparsest k-Subgraph, Graph Partitioning), and showing multi-angle QAOA outperforms shared-angle variants on the tested instances.
methodology_description: The authors analyze the dynamical Lie algebras (DLAs) of parameterized circuits built from XY-type two-qubit mixers (path, cycle, clique topologies) with and without single-qubit Z and two-qubit ZZ phase/separator terms, and use that analysis to motivate a warm-starting strategy for QAOA-style variational quantum algorithms applied to cardinality-constrained combinatorial optimization. They perform numerical experiments (classical simulation) comparing warm-started circuits against randomly initialized circuits on three problem families (portfolio optimization using S&P500 data, sparsest k-subgraph, and graph partitioning). The restricted (pretrain) ansatz uses XY-cycle mixers plus single-qubit RZ phase separators (no RZZ), which the authors show has a polynomial-sized DLA; the full ansatz adds the RZZ phase separators and generally has an exponentially large DLA. The warm-start procedure: (1) restrict the gate set to the polynomially trainable sub-algebra and randomly initialize its angles in [0,2π]; (2) pretrain that restricted circuit (they report 100 optimization steps); (3) transfer learned angles into the full circuit by setting the additional RZZ gate angles to zero; (4) refine/train the full circuit (they report 100 optimization steps). Training is performed with the Adam optimizer in the PennyLane framework. Initial states are Dicke states (uniform superposition over fixed Hamming weight k = n/2), the loss is the expectation value of the problem Hamiltonian H_f (embedded into Z and ZZ terms), and evaluations report approximation ratio and success probability. Experiments sweep circuit depth p (examples up to p=40 reported), qubit counts n={12,14,16} (for portfolio experiments), and use multiple random restarts (best-of-10 per instance) with summary statistics (median, quartiles) over instance ensembles (84 monthly S&P500 instances for portfolio task, and ensembles of random/regular graphs for the other problems).
algorithms_used: Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz (QAOA with tailored XY mixers)
experimental_setup: Classical numerical simulation of parameterized quantum circuits using the PennyLane framework. Circuits use Dicke-state initialization (|D_n^{n/2}>), XY two-qubit mixers (cycle topology for restricted pretraining), RZ single-qubit phase separators, and optional RZZ two-qubit phase separators for the full ansatz. Training performed with the Adam optimizer. Depths p scanned (examples up to p=40); qubit sizes reported include n=12, 14, 16. Pretraining of restricted ansatz for 100 optimization steps, transfer parameters (set RZZ angles to zero), then refine full circuit for 100 steps. Best-of-10 random restarts per instance; report medians and quartiles over instance ensembles.
dataset_used: S&P 500 historical trading data (public) aggregated into monthly instances (84 months between 2010 and 2018) to build returns and covariance inputs for portfolio optimization. Additional synthetic graph instance sets: random graphs with ~2n edges and 3-regular random graphs used for graph partitioning and sparsest k-subgraph experiments.

pipeline: Tailor ansatz: pick mixer set M (e.g. XY-cycle) and phase separators N (subset of Z and optionally ZZ).
Construct restricted (pretrain) circuit U_WS with M = XY-cycle and N = GZ (single-qubit RZ only). Parameter vector θ_WS ∈ R^{2 n p} (n XY + n RZ per layer).
Randomly initialize θ_WS_i uniformly in [0, 2π] for pretraining.
Pretrain restricted circuit: optimize θ_WS to minimize expectation ⟨Dicke| U_WS(θ_WS)† H_f U_WS(θ_WS) |Dicke⟩ using the Adam optimizer for 100 steps.
Transfer parameters: set full-circuit parameters θ_init := (θ_WS_f, 0) — i.e., copy pre-trained XY and RZ angles, initialize RZZ angles to zero.
Refine full circuit U(θ) (including RZZ gates) by optimizing θ with Adam for 100 steps to minimize same loss.
Compare to baseline: randomly initialize full circuit angles in [0,2π] and optimize for same number of steps.
Repeat per instance with multiple random restarts (10 in reported experiments) and record metrics per run. Aggregate across instance ensembles reporting median and quartiles.
Sweep circuit depth p (examples include p up to 40) and qubit count n (examples n∈{12,14,16}).

key_findings: [supported] The dynamical Lie algebra (DLA) of 1D XY-mixer topologies (path and cycle) decomposes into polynomial-sized Lie algebras (so(n) and su(n) components) — e.g. g_P_XY(n) ≅ so(n), g_C_XY(n) ≅ so(n)⊕so(n) for even n and ≅ su(n) for odd n.

[supported] Adding single-qubit Z rotations (RZ) to 1D XY cycle/path gives DLAs that remain polynomial-sized and decompose into su(n) and u(1) components (e.g. g_P_XY,Z(n) ≅ u(1)⊕su(n); g_C_XY,Z(n) ≅ u(1)⊕su(n)⊕su(n)).

[supported] Including all-to-all XY connectivity (clique) or adding two-qubit ZZ interactions (RZZ) causes the DLA to grow exponentially in n (proved lower bounds Ω(3^n); conjectured full scaling ~4^n/ poly(n)).

[supported] There is a direct connection (from literature and analysis here) between DLA dimension and trainability: polynomial-sized DLAs avoid barren-plateau pathology and are more efficiently trainable; exponential DLAs correlate with barren plateaus (vanishing gradients).

[supported] A warm-starting strategy that (1) restricts the gate-set to a polynomial-sized DLA (cycle XY + RZ), (2) pretrains this restricted ansatz, and (3) transfers parameters to the full ansatz (turning on RZZ) improves QAOA training convergence and solution quality in the reported numerical experiments.

[supported] The warm-starting approach produced systematically better approximation ratios and higher success probabilities than random initialization on numerical instances of Portfolio Optimization (SP500 monthly instances), Sparsest k-Subgraph, and Graph Partitioning for n up to 16 in the experiments reported.
[supported] Multi-angle QAOA (MA-QAOA) empirically outperformed shared-angle QAOA (SA-QAOA) on the considered constrained-optimization instances in these experiments.

[speculative] The full decomposition of the clique (all-to-all) XY-mixer DLA is given by a direct sum over Hamming-weight subspace su(d_k) components (conjectured forms in the paper); they conjecture g_K_XY,Z and g_C_XY,Z,ZZ contain the maximal algebra commuting with total Z (up to centers).

[speculative] The authors conjecture exact asymptotic DLA dimension scalings for clique and RZZ-including cases (claimed 4^n − Θ(log n)), based on small-n computations and algebraic arguments but not proven fully in the manuscript.

[supported] Theoretical proofs/sketches are given for the polynomial-sized DLA decompositions (path and cycle cases) and for the existence of exponentially many independent generators in clique/RZZ cases (lower bounds).

[supported] The authors provide an explicit warm-start procedural prescription (restrict→pretrain→transfer→refine) and applied it in numerical experiments using Adam optimization within PennyLane simulations.
[supported] The paper notes limitations: warm-start benefits may diminish on adversarial instances or scale differently at larger n; the authors do not claim universal superiority.
results_summary: This preprint analyzes dynamical Lie algebras (DLAs) arising from typical XY-mixer topologies used in QAOA-style constrained optimization. For 1D topologies (path and cycle) — including when single-qubit Z rotations are allowed — the DLAs decompose into polynomially-sized Lie algebras (so(n), su(n) and u(1) components), which are theoretically benign for training. In contrast, all-to-all XY connectivity or adding arbitrary ZZ interactions produces exponentially large DLAs (proved lower bounds and conjectured full decompositions), which correlate with barren-plateau trainability issues. Motivated by these algebraic findings, the authors propose and numerically validate a warm-starting strategy: pretrain a restricted ansatz within the polynomial DLA (cycle XY + RZ), transfer parameters into the full ansatz, then refine. Numerical experiments on Portfolio Optimization (SP500 monthly instances), Sparsest k-Subgraph, and Graph Partitioning (n up to 16) show consistent improvements in approximation ratio and success probability versus random initialization. The paper supplies theoretical proofs for the polynomial cases, lower bounds for exponential growth cases, and conjectures for full clique decompositions.
performance_claims: g_P_XY(n) ≅ so(n) with dimension n(n−1)/2 (polynomial in n) [supported]
g_C_XY(n) ≅ so(n)⊕so(n) for even n (dimension n(n−1)) and ≅ su(n) for odd n (dimension n^2−1) [supported]
g_P_XY,Z(n) ≅ u(1)⊕su(n) (dimension n^2) and g_C_XY,Z(n) ≅ u(1)⊕su(n)⊕su(n) (dimension 2n^2−1) [supported]

Inclusion of nearest-neighbor ZZ or full RZZ or full XY-clique yields DLAs of size at least Ω(3^n) (reported lower bound) and conjectured full scaling ≈ 4^n/ poly(n) [supported (lower bound) / speculative (full scaling)]

Empirical: Warm-started MA-QAOA produced higher median approximation ratios and higher median success probabilities than random initialization across reported instances (SP500 monthly instances, and graph problems) for n∈{12,14,16} and depths up to p≤40 — qualitative improvement shown in figures [supported].
Empirical: MA-QAOA outperformed SA-QAOA on the considered problem instances in the experiments [supported].
quantum_advantage_detail: The paper does not claim a demonstrated quantum computational advantage. It studies algebraic structure (DLAs) of mixer topologies, implications for trainability, and proposes a warm-starting method that improves variational training in classical simulations. Results are improvements in optimizer convergence and solution quality for QAOA-style circuits in simulation, not proof of outperforming classical algorithms or demonstrating quantum advantage.
limitations: Some central DLA decomposition claims (especially for fully-connected/clique topologies and certain RZ/RZZ-inclusive cases) are stated as conjectures and lack formal proofs.
Empirical verification of large-DLA conjectures is limited to small n; scaling and asymptotic behavior are not rigorously established.
The presence of exponential-sized DLAs (e.g., all-to-all XY or inclusion of RZZ) implies Barren Plateau risks and makes training intractable in those settings.
Warm-starting results are empirical on selected instance families (Portfolio Optimization, Sparsest k-Subgraph, Graph Partitioning) and may not generalize to all problem instances.
[inferred] Warm-starting improvement may degrade for much larger instance sizes than those numerically studied (authors note this possibility).

[inferred] Warm-starting uses a restriction that removes gates (e.g., RZZ); the effectiveness depends on finding a restriction that is both meaningful and yields a polynomial-sized DLA, which may not exist for all problems or hardware topologies.
Numerical experiments use classical simulation (Pennylane, Adam) and are limited to moderate qubit counts (examples shown for n up to 16), so practical performance on noisy hardware is untested here.
Code and data are not publicly bundled; they are available only upon request, which limits immediate reproducibility.

#idea:near-term-feasibility — DLA analysis motivates NISQ-friendly ansatz design: 1D path/cycle XY mixers with single-qubit Z rotations have polynomial-sized DLAs (efficiently trainable), while all-to-all XY connectivity or adding RZZ terms yields exponentially large DLAs (harder to train), suggesting practical restricted subspaces for near-term devices.
